surface: The stop: a commitment at its hour
where: The dialog when any way of moving the clock reaches a commitment: Go, Stand Here, and the choices the commitment's kind offers (Skip It on a plan of your own, Call It Off on a rehearsal with a partner)
why: Read at a plan of your own from 11:30 PM to 12:30 AM on the way to Tomorrow Morning (brief 19's walk, before and after): the stop offered Skip It and said nothing of what it does to the jump, which carried on, while Call It Off on a partner's rehearsal ended the jump, also unsaid (brief 18's S1). Both carry the jump on now (`carryOnTo`), and the stop says so before the press; a refused choice leaves the stop open and says why. The developer's error for a kind declared twice is never shown to a player.
changes: A plan's stop gained "Skip It marks your plan missed, at no cost but the plan, and the clock carries on to August 28, 2026 at 7:00 AM, stopping at the next commitment on the way. Stand Here keeps the clock paused here, and Meet Sam At The Station starts the next time it moves."; a partner's rehearsal "Call It Off calls the rehearsal off, and the clock carries on to …"; a refused Skip It's words are the refusal's own ("That’s already over: it was kept, missed or called off."), with the stop kept open.

evidence.ref: tests/time-controls.test.ts: 'PLAYER JOURNEY: On The Way names Skip It and that the jump carries on'
tests/time-controls.test.ts: 'a Skip It that’s refused leaves the stop open, the clock where it stopped, and says why'
tests/time-stops.test.ts: 'PLAYER JOURNEY: Call It Off on a partner’s rehearsal'

where: The dialog before an Advance line passes a commitment
why: Read before Tomorrow Morning with two plans on the way, and before One Week from a Friday evening (brief 14's banking journey, step 8): it named Skip It and Call It Off whatever was on the way, never said the jump carries on after either, and from a Friday didn't open at all, since the next week's classes go on the calendar the Sunday before. It names the choices of the commitments it lists now, and what the jump does after them, and lists the stops the jump will make that aren't on the calendar yet (`onTheWay`).
changes: "You can also skip a plan of your own, or call off a rehearsal with a partner, though at short notice that costs their trust." became the choices of what's listed ("You can also skip a plan of your own, and the clock then carries on."); a commitment not on the calendar yet reads "Classes — August 31, 2026 at 9:00 AM, not on your calendar yet", with "What isn’t on your calendar yet goes on it as the clock moves, before it comes." under the list.

evidence.ref: tests/time-controls.test.ts: 'PLAYER JOURNEY: On The Way lists the next week’s classes, not on the calendar yet'
tests/language-frame-ui.test.ts: 'On The Way says how many commitments the clock stops at and what each stop offers, for one and for two'

where: Advance, then Choose An Event…: each event's count of what's on the way, and the picked one's list
why: Read from a Friday evening: an event after Monday counted nothing on the way, though the jump to it stops at Monday's classes, which the School puts on the calendar on Sunday. The count and the list now hold those stops too, foreseen up to a month ahead, each marked not on the calendar yet; a commitment the clock is standing at, which the jump runs at once, isn't counted.
changes: A foreseen stop is listed as "Classes — August 31, 2026, not on your calendar yet", and counted in its event's "N on the way".

evidence.ref: tests/time-controls.test.ts: 'Skip To Event counts them on the way to a later event'

where: The top bar's Advance: each line and where it lands
why: Read at 2:00 AM after a stop: Tomorrow Morning said "7:00 AM · August 29, 2026", a whole day on, and went there past Friday's ten o'clock (brief 18's S2). It goes to the next seven now (`nextAtHour`), and each line gives the weekday and date with the time, so the day is said before the press.
changes: "Tomorrow Morning 7:00 AM · August 29, 2026" at 2 AM became "Tomorrow Morning 7:00 AM · Friday, August 28, 2026"; One Hour, which gave a time alone, and One Week, "September 3, 2026 at 11:00 PM", give the day the same way.

evidence.ref: tests/time-controls.test.ts: 'at 2 AM Tomorrow Morning says seven that Friday and lands there'

where: The top bar's Sleep: the dialog's suggestion and its reason
why: Read at 7:15 AM up from eight hours, and at 11:00 PM before a ten o'clock commitment (brief 19's walk, before and after): at 7:15 it said "A normal night." and 8 hours, to 3:15 PM (brief 18's S3), and the clock ran on behind it (S4). A sleep on a day whose night is behind it is a nap now, said with the energy that decides it; a commitment's own trip is kept back before it; at 11 PM it's the normal night it was. The dialog holds the clock while it's open.
changes: At 7:15 AM "A normal night." (8 hours) became "You’ve already slept since midnight, and with your energy at 100 you don’t need more sleep yet. A sleep under six hours adds to the sleep you owe, so it’s best kept for the night." (half an hour); low, "… but your energy is down to 18. Seven and a half hours would bring it back to full."; cut by a commitment, "“Breakfast With Sam” is in 3 hours. Getting up and there takes an hour and a half, so there’s time for one and a half hours. …"; with a trip, "Getting up takes an hour, and getting there 2 hours and 30 minutes, so there isn’t time for a full night."

evidence.ref: tests/time-stops.test.ts: 'PLAYER JOURNEY: at 7:15 AM, up from a night, suggests no more sleep and says why'
tests/time-stops.test.ts: 'keeps back the commitment’s own trip'
tests/time-controls.test.ts: 'PLAYER JOURNEY: with the Sleep dialog open a minute passes and the clock and the save don’t move'

surface: The guide on the clock, moving time on and sleep
where: The chapters What's Coming, The Clock, Moving Time On and Sleep, and How This Works for The Calendar, The Clock: Play And Pause, Moving Time On and Sleep
why: Checked against the game as brief 19 left it: The Calendar said Call It Off left the clock paused, where it carries the jump on; The Clock said the Sleep dialog doesn't stop the clock, where it, On The Way and Skip To Event hold it; Moving Time On listed Tomorrow Morning after midnight going a whole day on as a mistake to avoid, where it goes to that morning's seven; Sleep said the suggestion came from when you're next needed and the sleep you owe, kept an hour and a half for everything, and that what's on the calendar while you sleep happens without you, where a commitment slept through is missed.
changes: Each of those said as the game does it now: Skip It and Call It Off carry the jump on; the dialogs that move the clock hold it; each Advance line gives its day, and On The Way lists what isn't on the calendar yet; the suggestion reads whether the night's behind you, your energy and the commitment's own trip; a commitment slept through is missed.

evidence.ref: tests/help-mechanics.test.ts: 'PLAYER JOURNEY: Stand Here ends the jump at the commitment with the clock paused, and Go carries it on, as Moving Time On says'
